clusters.headline_hint: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 as son Haakon VIII ascends the throne

claims.text: King Harald V of Norway died on August 28 at the age of 89 after a reign of 35 years.
King Harald V's 53-year-old son immediately succeeded him on the throne as King Haakon VIII.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store stated in a speech, 'An era has ended. A new one begins. The king is dead. Long live the king.'
King Harald V had been hospitalized in Oslo since August 17 suffering from haemolytic anaemia.
The Norwegian Armed Forces honoured King Harald V with a 21-shot funeral salute from Akershus Fortress in central Oslo.
King Haakon VIII's 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra became the new crown princess and next in line to the throne.
Britain's King Charles III paid tribute to King Harald V, describing him as a 'towering figure' who guided Norway with 'warmth and humility.'
A poll in February showed public support for Norway's monarchy dropped to 54% from 72% in 2024.
Crown Princess Mette-Marit's son, Marius Borg Hoiby, was sentenced in June to four years in prison following a rape conviction.

clusters.headline_hint: Trump announces deal securing US majority control of 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves

claims.text: US President Donald Trump announced an agreement with Venezuela securing US control over more than 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's proven oil reserves.
Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez stated the oil deal involves developing 17 strategic oil fields, drawing over $100 billion in investment and generating over $209 billion in state taxes.
A US official stated that under the deal, the US government retains 55% effective control of a joint venture with a private operator granted a 100-year concession in Venezuela.
Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were captured by US special forces on January 3.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that the Venezuela oil deal would bring nearly $100 billion in private investment and support thousands of high-paying jobs.
The US Strategic Petroleum Reserve dropped below 300 million barrels in early August, decreasing by over 100 million barrels since early 2026.
The average price of petrol in the US reached $4.09 a gallon on August 28, compared to $3.21 a year earlier.

clusters.headline_hint: Israeli drone strike in West Bank town of Jenin kills three Palestinian militants

claims.text: An Israeli drone strike killed three Palestinians in Jenin, marking the first Israeli military air strike in the West Bank since February 2025.
The Israeli military stated it eliminated three militants in Jenin, identifying one as Hamas operative Qais Bitawi.
Palestinian Islamic Jihad stated that Qais Bitawi and two others killed in the Jenin strike were its fighters, identifying Bitawi as a leader in the Al-Quds Brigades.
The Palestinian Red Crescent stated Israeli forces briefly detained its medical crews at the strike site and confiscated their equipment.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz posted on X, 'These are the fruits of the aggressive and proactive policy we are leading in the West Bank: we do not wait for terror – we pursue it, conquer its strongholds and thwart its people.'

clusters.headline_hint: Meta agrees to $18 billion settlement and introduces youth safety protections on Instagram and Facebook

claims.text: Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement with US states and territories, ending a federal lawsuit over allegations its social media platforms harmed children's mental health.
Meta agreed to implement a combined default daily screen-time limit of two hours across Facebook and Instagram for accounts belonging to minors.
Meta will introduce an automatic night mode blocking minor profiles from Feeds, Stories, Reels, and Explore pages between midnight and 6:00 am.
Meta's new 'School Mode' will default to muting standard push notifications for teenage users between 8:00 am and 3:00 pm.
Meta announced it will withhold $5 billion of its $18 billion settlement until rival platforms like TikTok and YouTube enter into similar youth protection agreements.

clusters.headline_hint: Greenland establishes truth commission over historic Danish forced contraception campaign

claims.text: Greenland announced the creation of a Truth and Reconciliation Commission to examine a historical forced contraception campaign against Indigenous Inuit women and girls.
A joint inquiry revealed that between the 1960s and 1990s, at least 4,000 Greenlandic Inuits were fitted with IUDs or received contraceptive injections without informed consent.
The Danish parliament approved compensation payments of up to 300,000 Danish crowns ($46,758) for each woman affected by the forced contraception program.
A four-member expert panel appointed to investigate Greenland's forced contraception campaign split and submitted two conflicting reports on whether the actions constituted genocide.
Panel experts Dalee Sambo Dorough and Miriam Cullen determined that Inuit women's rights were violated but stated they could not conclude genocide occurred based on contraceptive practices alone.
By the late 1970s, at least 4,070 women—representing one out of every two Greenlandic women of childbearing age—had been fitted with an IUD.

clusters.headline_hint: Devastating Nepal-Tibet flash floods leave over 500 dead and thousands missing, prompting Indian relief and rescue operations

claims.text: Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal stated that Nepal needs foreign technical assistance for specialized tasks such as tunnel rescue, body identification, DNA testing, and body storage.
A glacier collapse on Wednesday triggered flash floods that killed nearly 600 people across Nepal and Tibet, leaving over 2,400 missing.
Nepal's official death toll from the flash floods reached 579, while Chinese state media reported seven deaths in Tibet.
Chinese authorities evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet following the floods.
At least 2,478 people were reported missing after the flood, including 1,924 in Nepal and 554 in Tibet.
More than 3,700 people have been rescued in Nepal, while at least 93,000 people have been affected by the calamity according to the Red Cross.
India sent 62 tonnes of emergency relief assistance to Nepal across three airlifts following the disaster.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah shortly after the disaster to offer humanitarian assistance.
The United Arab Emirates allocated $10 million in humanitarian aid to Nepal through the UAE Aid Agency.
Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle stated that Nepal will require at least a few billion dollars to recover from the flood destruction.
Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar received 21 pilgrims from Tamil Nadu who were rescued from flood-affected areas in Nepal.
At least 320 Indian nationals remained uncontactable in Nepal following the flash floods.
Official sources stated that 149 Indian nationals crossed over from China into Nepal on August 28, 2026.

clusters.headline_hint: Karnataka Minister B. Nagendra resigns over Valmiki Corporation financial irregularities

claims.text: Karnataka Minister B. Nagendra submitted his resignation on Friday, 25 days after being re-inducted into the state cabinet.
Nagendra faces opposition allegations regarding the alleged misappropriation of ₹89 crore from the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation.
B. Nagendra requested permission from the Congress leadership to resign as an MLA in addition to stepping down from his cabinet position.
The financial irregularities in the Valmiki Corporation surfaced in May 2024 after an accounts superintendent died by suicide and left a note alleging unauthorized fund transfers.
Nagendra had previously resigned as tribal welfare minister in June 2024 before being re-inducted into the cabinet on August 3 after D.K. Shivakumar became Chief Minister.
Announcing his resignation, B. Nagendra stated: "Today I am voluntarily tendering my resignation as the minister."
Protests by opposition parties over Nagendra's cabinet return led to the Karnataka Legislature's monsoon session being adjourned sine die on August 24.
Police took BJP leaders B.Y. Vijayendra and R. Ashoka into preventive custody during a protest march toward the Vidhana Soudha in Bengaluru.

clusters.headline_hint: FSSAI proposes front-of-pack red warning labels for packaged food high in fat, sugar, and salt

claims.text: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) filed a compliance affidavit with the Supreme Court proposing red hexagonal warning labels on the front of packaged foods.
The front-of-pack labelling case stems from a public interest litigation filed in the Supreme Court by the NGO 3S and Our Health Society.
Single-ingredient foods such as ghee, edible oil, salt, sugar, jaggery, and honey are proposed to be exempted from the front-of-pack warning requirement.

The proposed warning labels will display terms like 'High Fat', 'High Sugar', 'High Salt', or 'Highly Sweetened Beverage' in a font size one point larger than the nutrition table on the back of the package.
A Supreme Court bench headed by Justice J.B. Pardiwala issued an order on August 13 giving the government two weeks to submit its final decision on front-of-pack nutrition labelling.
A study published in The Lancet estimated that roughly 450 million people in India could be overweight or obese by 2050.
FSSAI proposed implementing the warning labels in two phases, starting with foods high in two or more specified nutrients before extending to foods high in any single specified nutrient.
The proposed labelling thresholds are based on the Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024 issued by the ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition.
Senior Coca-Cola India executive Mili Bhattacharya stated during a March 19 meeting that it is "very simplistic" to believe seeing a symbol on a label will significantly improve a consumer's diet.

clusters.headline_hint: India to acquire Javelin anti-tank missile system from United States

claims.text: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor announced that India plans to purchase the Javelin anti-tank guided missile system from the United States.
The Javelin is a man-portable anti-tank missile that uses fire-and-forget technology to track and hit targets automatically after launch.
The proposed sale of the Javelin anti-tank missile system to India is valued at $45.7 million.
US Ambassador Sergio Gor noted that US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth raised the possibility of joint co-production of the Javelin system at the May 2026 Shangri-La Dialogue.
In November 2025, the US State Department approved a potential $93 million sale to India involving up to 100 Javelin systems and 216 Excalibur artillery projectiles.
India requested to buy 100 FGM-148 Javelin rounds, one fly-to-buy missile, and 25 Javelin Command Launch Units.
India signed a Letter of Offer and Acceptance with the United States to purchase the Javelin anti-tank guided missile system through Foreign Military Sales.
The Javelin anti-tank missile system has been in full-rate production since 1994 and reached its 50,000th delivery in 2021.
